newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends steady in Tokyo, awaits FOMC.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends steady in Tokyo, awaits FOMC.

text.p: The key three-month Euroyen deposit rate contract ended Tuesday's day session unchanged as traders were reluctant to take large positions ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later today.

"Given the current market atmosphere, if the Fed does not tighten, the market will become even more bullish, and the market is unlikely to be depressed for long even if it does tighten slightly," said a city bank trader.
More funds are likely to be shifted from the short-term sector to longer-term securities, such as Japanese Government Bonds and U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
Shoji Kitta, managing director of Japan's largest money broker Tokyo Tanshi Co Ltd, estimated such funds would total seven to eight trillion yen.
This is partly because of the slow demand for bank loans, which could also be a beneficiary of the pooled funds in the money market, he said.
The benchmark three month certificates of deposit were at 0.53 percent, unchanged since September 3.
